Nwaneri steps up with the chance to win the shootout and does so with aplomb, sending Meyer the wrong way, and Arsenal win the shootout 5-4.

The former Chelsea man receives some boos as he steps up but calmly slots home to keep Dortmund’s hopes alive.

Meyer goes the right way but there is far too much power on this penalty from Martinelli. Meyer had no chance of saving that one.

We have the first penalty miss of this shootout as Meslier guesses the right way and saves what was a pretty poor penalty from Albert. Advantage Arsenal.

A few stutters in the run-up but Hincapie slots home into the bottom left corner, with Meyer going the wrong way.

He came on right at the end of the game to take a penalty and rewards the decision from his manager to do so as he lifts it over Meslier diving to his left.

Another penalty scored in the left corner. Meyer again guesses the right way but cannot prevent Vieira.

There is a bit of a stutter in the run-up as Reggiani stares down Meslier and sends the Arsenal keeper the wrong way, finding the same corner as Sabitzer and Jesus.

Meyer in the Dortmund goal guesses the right way but Jesus lifts it over him with a quality penalty.

Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

Right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

Arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

It is perhaps not a massive surprise but the game has lost some flow with all the changes both sides have made during this second half.

There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:

With just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

The Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

Nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

In the aftermath of that Dortmund goal, there are a raft of changes for both sides. Arsenal have brought on Salmon and Hincapie for Calafiori and Gabriel.

Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

Arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

Should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

Mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

That is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

White is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

Dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

Dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

During half-time at the Emirates, the official song of the 2026 Fifa World Cup Dai Dai by Shakira and Burna Boy is being belted out over the tannoy. The World Cup final was exactly three weeks ago today, with three of Arsenal’s players in Spain’s winning squad; David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi.

Konstantinos Karetsas has arrived. 🇬🇷🇬🇷🇬🇷 pic.twitter.com/nI4A7KPT4o

The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

Gabriel is into the book. He is in possession but his touch allows the ball to slightly get away from him. He then slides in to try and retain possession and catches Karetsas.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Nmecha eyes up a repeat of Dortmund’s first goal as he tries to find the run of Inacio into the Arsenal box but this time they cannot quite link up.

After Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

Arsenal want a penalty but the appeals are turned down. It all stems from good work defensively from Tzolis, who drives forward from the edge of his own box and then finds Gyokeres out to his left. Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

Tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

With it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

What a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

Odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

Should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

Odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

Gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

Calafiori trips Bellingham as Dortmund attempted to counter. If this was a competitive fixture, Calafiori likely would have been booked for that foul.

Bellingham and Havertz are involved in quite the collision. Both players go for the header and Havertz just gets to it first. Havertz is awarded the foul and is ok.

The German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area. It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,

Dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal issues and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

Gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

Just before the two sides emerge the tunnel, there is a special guest who comes out first in the form of Bruno Guimaraes. Chants of “Bruno! Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

Reports are that Jobe’s older brother Jude is at the Emirates today, not that Arsenal fans should think that Jude is swapping Real Madrid for the red half of north London.

Arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀

When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

#2140. James Trafford's old ghost returns to haunt him as Marco Rose's Bournemouth side claim another heavyweight scalp to make it six wins on the spin

Published: 13:23 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 16:56 EDT, 31 October 2026

How fitting it was, amid this season of werewolves and vampires, that it was one of James Trafford’s old ghosts that came back to haunt him.

No witches or zombies will give the Leeds goalkeeper a sleepless night quite like this familiar howler that cost his side the game.

The visitors dominated Bournemouth for most of the first half with confident, flowing football and thought they had a deserved lead when Dominic Calvert-Lewin bundled the ball into the net early on after a stunning passing move only for the goal to be ruled out for a handball.

Leeds were firmly on top…and then they had a goal-kick. Trafford didn’t take it but received it short and tried to pass it out to Ao Tanaka only to play it straight to the lurking Justin Kluivert, who squared it to Evanlison for a tap-in.

It was almost identical to the goal Trafford conceded at the Etihad Stadium against Tottenham at the start of last season, on his second league start for Manchester City, when he - again - received a short goal-kick and tried to pass it to a team-mate who was already surrounded. City signed Gianluigi Donnarumma 10 days later and Trafford’s City career was all-but over.

The England keeper has been able to resurrect it at Leeds, and came into the game with the best save percentage of any stopper in the Premier League, and marshaller of the second-best defence in the division behind only champions Arsenal.

Trafford made a fine save from a Marcus Tavernier free-kick, and another effort late on from Junior Kroupi but the damage had been done. He could do little about Amine Adli’s finish that doubled Bournemouth’s lead in second-half stoppage time. The Bournemouth supporters, who jeered him every time he touched the ball, made sure he didn’t forget it.

‘James is a terrific young goalkeeper,’ said Leeds boss Daniel Farke. ‘I’m pretty sure he will save us way more points than he perhaps has cost us today. We win together, we lose together. We’re all happy to have him. He’s still top class and has all my trust and all my love. My recommendation is that he shouldn’t watch the scene back!’

It was almost identical to the goal Trafford conceded against Tottenham at the start of last season when he - again - received a short goal-kick and passed it straight to the opposition

The English goalkeeper could do little about Amine Adli’s finish that doubled Bournemouth’s lead in second-half stoppage time

Bournemouth have made such a habit of punching above their weight in recent years, that victories over traditional Premier League big boys no longer seem as remarkable as they once did. Running your club brilliantly, signing excellent players and developing them with superb coaches season after season will tend to normalise such success for a club of this size.

The Cherries are no longer content to constrain their heroics to slaying mere domestic giants. In the space of 10 days, they have dispatched former European Cup winners AC Milan, Manchester United and Aston Villa — all 3-0 — and now former runners-up Leeds.

Yes, they needed a bit of luck and a glaring mistake to get them ahead but, once they got in front, they rarely looked like letting it slip. Brazilian sensation Rayan went close before substitute Adli wrapped it up late on after a stunning through ball from Kroupi.

Bournemouth needed a bit of luck and a glaring mistake to get them ahead but, once they got in front, they rarely looked like letting it slip

Bournemouth (4-2-3-1): Petrovic 7; Smith 7 (Diakite 88), Hill 8, Silva 7, Truffert 6; Adams 7, Christie 7 (Cook 6); Rayan 6 (Adli 88), Kluivert 7 (Kroupi 68, 8), Tavernier 7; EVANILSON 8 (Rodriguez 76).

Leeds (3-4-2-1): Trafford 5; Justin 6 (Bahoya 84), Elvedi 6, Muharemovic 7; Bogle 6, Ampadu 6, Tanaka 5 (Stach 65, 6); Gudmudsson 6 (Longstaff 65, 5); Wilson 6 (Aaronson 84), James 7 (Nmecha 65, 6); Calvert-Lewin 6.

What is even more impressive is that Bournemouth are doing it without Andoni Iraola at the helm, and under a manager in Marco Rose who was even feeling early grumblings of discontent from sections of the fanbase after failing to win any of their first six league games.

Now, it’s six wins in a row in all competitions. Sixteen goals scored, none conceded. Even for Bournemouth, who make the remarkable look normal, that’s quite something.

Not only that, they are doing it without influential midfielder Alex Scott, out with a hamstring injury, pulling the strings. When you have Ryan Christie and Tyler Adams keeping things ticking in the middle, with Justin Kluivert and Kroupi ahead of them, you barely even noticed.

Marco Rose was feeling early grumblings of discontent from sections of the fanbase after failing to win any of their first six league games

We’re approaching that time of year, with Halloween already upon us and Christmas coming into view, when the constant churn of January transfer rumours will soon become inescapable.

An early one doing the rounds is how Manchester United are ‘exploring a move’ for Calvert-Lewin.

Don’t fall for it, Dominic. He lost here but how different the afternoon could have gone had the ball not bounced on to his arm before going into the net. Even in defeat, this is still a club under Daniel Farke that’s stable, competent and moving in the right direction.

If United are really in the market for someone who knows where the net is, few are doing it with more ruthless efficiency than Bournemouth striker Evanlison, who made it four goals in as many games for the Cherries.

‘I just saw him said: “You are a real number 9”,’ said Bournemouth boss Marco Rose.

#2139. Man Utd told £50m offer could tempt Fulham to sell highly rated teenager

Manchester United could face an expensive battle to sign Fulham youngster Josh King, with offers exceeding £50million potentially enough to persuade the London club to consider a sale.

The 19-year-old has attracted attention with his performances this season, despite Fulham’s difficult results.

Manchester United are among several clubs monitoring his progress, alongside Liverpool, Arsenal, Borussia Dortmund and Barcelona.

Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, Pete O’Rourke explained that King’s growing reputation has put him on the radar of several major clubs.

“Josh King will be on the radar for a number of clubs because of his performances for Fulham so far this season,” O’Rourke said.

“It’s not just Liverpool, there’s been talk of the likes of Manchester United, Arsenal, Borussia Dortmund and even Barcelona looking at Josh King.”

Fulham are not actively planning to let the teenager leave in the near future as he is under contract until 2029. The contract length gives Fulham an upper hand, while interest from multiple clubs indicates a concession is not expected.

“Fulham are not planning for any early departure for Josh King. He is still under contract until 2029, and obviously they’ll want to keep him.”

The reporter also pointed to Fulham’s league position as a factor that could influence their decision. If they become embroiled in a relegation battle, losing one of their best performers would be a major risk.

“If Manchester United or any other club wanted to make an offer, he’s going to be worth in excess of £50million probably right now.”

#2138. Why must Manchester United move beyond the Glazers?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Glazers took control of Manchester United in 2005. That takeover has since caused so many disruptions and protests by the fans over massive debts and insufficient backing of the team in the transfer market, despite successful periods in the Premier League and Europe.

Now Manchester United need to think about who should control the club in the future. Laurie Whitwell has now shared his views on why Manchester United need an ownership change. He simply wants the Glazers gone from Old Trafford. However, he also recognizes that replacing the current ownership doesn’t automatically mean things will improve for United.

The journalist believes the change in ownership has had a lasting effect on United, with the club still feeling its consequences today. A fresh start might be welcome, but the identity of the next owners would matter just as much as the departure of the existing ones.

“Personally, I would like to see the Glazers gone from Manchester United,” Laurie Whitwell said on The Rest is Football podcast with Gary Lineker.

“That change, you know, just really affected and still impacts United now.”

The desire for different ownership is one thing, but finding people capable of taking the club forward is another.

Whitwell admitted there is no perfect answer when it comes to who should take charge.

That leaves United facing a difficult choice. A sale could offer the chance to change how the club is run, but simply bringing in a new owner would not guarantee better decisions or a brighter future.

Whitwell also raised the idea of United supporters having a greater say in the club’s ownership and decisions, much like the Barcelona model where fans own the club itself. However, he highlighted that the Barcelona model isn’t ideal either and has its own shortcomings.

Changing the names at the top would only be one part of the change. The club would also need an ownership structure capable of making sound decisions and providing a direction.

The issue of ownership goes beyond whether the Glazers should stay or leave. Manchester United needs to find the right people and the right model to secure the club’s future. Getting that decision wrong could leave them facing the same circus the fans are enduring under the Glazers.

#2137. 8 players set to miss Wrexham vs Middlesbrough ft £4.3m ace

The Championship season is now in full swing as we enter November, and midweek action is back on the agenda for the division's 24 clubs.

One of three second-tier offerings on Wednesday night is Wrexham's clash with high-flying Middlesbrough at the Racecourse Ground, with three points much-needed for both Phil Parkinson and Kim Hellberg, albeit for very differing reasons.

The Welsh side have been extremely below-par so far this term, and having lost three of their last four fixtures, pressure is firmly starting to build on Parkinson's shoulders with results nowhere near matching the club's lofty ambitions.

Boro, meanwhile, have been unstoppable in recent weeks, winning four of their last five and scoring 14 goals during that timeframe, including Saturday's 3-0 triumph over Charlton Athletic.

However, whilst both head coaches will be relying on the services of several star names to achieve a crucial victory, there are a total of eight players who are set to miss the encounter in total, and Football League World looks at all of their respective predicaments.

Sebastian Revan is the first of four players Wrexham are set to be without for Wednesday's encounter, with the defender still on the road to recovery from a serious hamstring issue.

The 23-year-old suffered such misfortune during his loan spell with Burton Albion last season, with his last competitive appearance for the Red Dragons coming all the way back in March 2025.

As such, Parkinson recently expressed his hopes that the left-back is fit enough to secure a loan move in the January window.

Fellow left-back, Liberato Cacace, has endured an injury-hit spell at the Racecourse Ground since joining from Empoli, with the New Zealand international still yet to feature this season.

Cacace, 26, featured at the FIFA World Cup three times after making just 13 appearances last term, with it being revealed that the defender continues to suffer recurring calf issues.

However, the timescale of his latest recovery is still not yet known.

Wrexham's poor start to the campaign has also coincided with an injury sustained by Welsh international forward, Nathan Broadhead, who posted 14 goal contributions last season.

Having featured in the opening three matches of the league season, the 28-year-old hasn't featured since due to a thigh injury which also ruled him out of Craig Bellamy's squad for the three-week international break between September and October.

Callum O'Hare missed Friday night's 1-0 defeat against his former club, Sheffield United, with a reported ankle issue, and remains a doubt ahead of the clash with Boro.

Wrexham paid £6.5m for the playmaker on Deadline Day in September, but he is yet to get off the mark for his new club in terms of goal contributions after netting in his final league appearance for the Blades.

However, in yet another cruel tale of misfortune for Parkinson, he revealed on Tuesday that Sam Smith will miss a prolonged period of action after sustaining a knee injury.

The striker replaced Ollie Rathbone at half-time, but after playing through the pain barrier in the game's latter stages, "his knee swelled up significantly the next day," said the Wrexham boss.

Smith, 28, will now see a specialist to learn the full extent of the setback.

The last absentee for Parkinson comes in the form of Josh Windass, whose experience and quality was vital in the club's play-off bid last season.

Windass has endured an injury-hit start to the season, having missed the entirety of pre-season and the competitive campaign's early weeks, and after just six appearances this term, was forced off in the early stages of the 1-1 draw at Derby County with an ankle issue.

The injury prognosis wasn't as bad as first envisaged though, albeit the 32-year-old has missed the subsequent four matches.

Alfie Jones is one of two players set to miss this encounter from the Middlesbrough camp, with the experienced Canadian international suffering more injury misfortune at the Riverside Stadium.

Having missed a fair chunk of his first season on Teesside, the 29-year-old suffered a blow to the calf in the dramatic 4-3 victory against Norwich City back in September.

It was expected that Jones would only miss a matter of weeks, before Hellberg revealed that he would be sidelined for longer due to an untimely setback.

The North East side also look set to be without summer signing, Rokas Pukstas, for a sixth successive encounter.

Having been recruited from Hadjuk Split for a reported £4.3m, the American youth international has played just six minutes of Championship football since his arrival, which came against Queens Park Rangers on September 5th.

Pukstas was then an unused substitute for three straight games before suffering a hamstring injury whilst partaking in private training, leaving him to miss, at least, the entirety of last month's action.

#2136. Fabrizio Romano shares latest on Martinez contract after explosive rant

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Argentinian defender has also apologized to the United higher ups as well over his comments, as shared by Fabrizio Romano.

Lisandro Martinez has held discussions with Jason Wilcox and Michael Carrick after speaking out following United’s 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Martinez had questioned whether Carrick was backed enough in the summer and suggested the club needed changes.

Fabrizio Romano has now confirmed that United consider the matter resolved for now and expect Martinez to remain available for selection.

Speaking about the situation on his YouTube channel, as quoted by Football 365, Romano explained why Martinez’s comments caused concern inside the club.

“He spoke very strongly after the game against Atletico Madrid, which Man Utd lost. It was a very negative moment for the Red Devils. We know that Licha was very strong in his comments. He said that Michael Carrick was not backed enough during the summer transfer window.”

Romano added that Martinez had spoken directly to those at the club after the incident.

“Licha apologised to Man Utd as a club. He spoke to the directors, he spoke to Jason Wilcox, and he spoke to Michael Carrick, who was also involved in this conversation.”

“So, the underlying message remains the same. Lisandro is apologising for the way he expressed himself after a game during a difficult moment for Man Utd, but there was a discussion about the substance of what he said.”

Romano also revealed that United had imposed a financial penalty on the centre-back. However, the punishment does not appear to involve removing him from the squad.

“According to the information available tonight, Lisandro Martinez has been fined.”

He added that Martinez is expected to return to the squad as normal, with the fine considered sufficient punishment for the incident.

“The internal discussion also helped to resolve all the issues. For Man Utd, the case is closed.”

That should bring some immediate clarity to the situation, although questions remain about how the episode could affect Martinez’s longer-term position at Old Trafford.

Romano also pointed towards Martinez’s contract, which expires next summer, with United holding an option to extend it.

“So, let’s see what is going to happen there. For sure, this is the kind of situation that will have an impact on the situation surrounding Lisandro, but we have to see what happens next in terms of future transfers and everything else.”

#2135. Will Lisandro Martinez play against Leeds after explosive rant?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Lisandro Martinez could return to Manchester United’s starting line-up against Leeds United this weekend, with the defender reportedly available for selection after the controversy surrounding his comments about the club’s summer transfer business.

TEAMtalk transfer insider Graeme Bailey has suggested Michael Carrick could bring the Argentine straight back into the team for the trip to Elland Road. The fixture is expected to be a hostile occasion, making Martinez’s potential involvement an interesting one.

“I am told that Martinez is available for selection this weekend, and there is every chance Michael Carrick starts him,” Bailey said.

The defender recently found himself in trouble after questioning whether Manchester United had done enough in the summer transfer window. He apologised to the club’s hierarchy and was fined, but the incident has not apparently created a divide between him and the manager.

Bailey also dismissed suggestions that Martinez’s comments were an attack on Michael Carrick, insisting the defender and his teammates continue to support the head coach.

“Martinez was not critical of Carrick – far from it. This isn’t a repeat of something like Mo Salah criticising Arne Slot last season. It is almost the opposite.”

According to Bailey, the United dressing room remains firmly behind Carrick despite the team’s disappointing start to the campaign. Senior players reportedly believe the current manager is still the right person to lead the team, rather than bringing in another face to replace him.

“Martinez and the squad are 100% behind Carrick. They know there is pressure after a poor start to the season, but they do not want to see a change.”

Bailey went on to suggest that the fallout may have strengthened the bond between the players and their manager.

“Martinez and the senior players firmly believe nobody can come in and do a better job than Carrick. If anything, this has brought the group closer together.”

The Robins were involved in a dramatic contest against Bolton Wanderers, but one in which they emerged on the right side of a 3-2 scoreline courtesy of Scott Twine's 93rd-minute winner, whilst Wanderers made it successive home victories with a dominant 3-0 win against Cardiff City.

As a result, Wolves moved up to third ahead of the midweek round of fixtures, just two points behind the automatic promotion places after 13 games, whilst a timely success for the West Country outfit saw them move up to 14th.

An entertaining game will be expected given the two sides have scored 38 goals between them so far this term, albeit 23 of those have come from the visitors.

However, as many as seven players could be unavailable to Michael Skubala and Cesar Peixoto.

Football League World ranks all 24 Championship clubs by the longest-serving member of their squad.

Skubala has revealed that the forward is "not too far off" a return, though.

#2133. The curious case of Joe Aribo as Rangers hero triggers comeback from football exile

Former Rangers hero Joe Aribo has been without a club since leaving Southampton in the summer following a loan spell at Leicester City.

It's a curious case for the former Ibrox maverick. Devastatingly effective on his day, yet clubless at the age of 30.

But Aribo is doing the opposite of giving in. He is currently putting in the hard yards in Dubai as he aims to reignite his career.

The midfielder's versatility was one of his greatest strengths, as he demonstrated by starting and scoring in the Europa League Final against Eintracht Frankfurt in Seville while operating as a makeshift false nine.

Aribo thrilled supporters during his time in Glasgow and went on to become an important player for Southampton, making 111 appearances for the Saints and sampling life in the Premier League.

Steven Gerrard adored him and Giovanni van Bronckhorst could scarcely do without him.

Now, however, Aribo finds himself on the outside looking in after the most frustrating period of his career.

Read more: Celtic supporter group demand Dermot Desmond end 20-year absence and attend AGM

Game time proved hard to come by at Southampton under Tonda Eckert and an ill-fated loan move to Leicester did little to improve matters. Minutes were scarce at the King Power and relegation only added to the disappointment.

For a player who once dazzled on European nights and played a leading role in one of Rangers' greatest modern runs, it has been a sobering fall from grace.

But the Nigeria international is now rested, recharged and desperate for another opportunity to prove he can still perform at the highest level.

The hard work is being done behind the scenes. Now Aribo is simply waiting on the chance to remind everyone why he was once one of the most coveted talents in Scottish football.

#2132. Leeds vs Man Utd preview: Team news, form, injuries and where to watch

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Leeds United welcome Manchester United to Elland Road on Sunday, with both sides looking to put a difficult run of results behind them and get their Premier League season on track.

Leeds United suffered a 2-1 defeat away to Arsenal last weekend despite James Justin scoring to put them in front in the 55th minute.

Manchester United also dropped points in the Premier League, drawing 1-1 with Tottenham, before losing 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League away from home.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to find consistency in recent weeks and have come under immense pressure to get in results. The Whites meanwhile will hope that home advantage can make the difference when United face their bitter rivals on Elland Road.

Leeds have recorded one win, two draws and two defeats in their last five matches in all competitions. Their best result came against Newcastle, where they won, but a 6-3 defeat to Chelsea in the Carabao Cup and the loss to Arsenal have left them searching for a response.

Manchester United have also won just once in their last five matches. Their 4-0 Champions League victory over Sabah FK was the only comfortable win, but defeats to Manchester City and Atletico Madrid, alongside draws against Fulham and Tottenham, have raised questions about their form and Michael Carrick.

Leeds are waiting on Dan James, who returned from international duty with a back problem and missed the Arsenal game. Joe Rodon remains sidelined with a hamstring injury and is not expected back in full training until next month. Harry Wilson could return after being an unused substitute last weekend. Mateo Joseph is also among Leeds’ absentees.

Manchester United have their own concerns. Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo are doubts after picking up issues against Tottenham and missing Tuesday’s trip to Madrid. Benjamin Sesko remains unavailable with a recurring shin problem, while Patrick Dorgu is expected to be out until late November. Manuel Ugarte is recovering from knee surgery, and Noussair Mazraoui is a doubt with a back problem.

There is better news regarding Matthijs de Ligt, who could return to contention. Leny Yoro is also available for selection despite his Champions League suspension.

The match takes place at Elland Road on Sunday, October 18. Kick-off is scheduled for 2 pm BST (1pm GMT).

UK viewers can watch the game live on Sky Sports Main Event, with coverage beginning at 1 pm BST.

#2130. Leeds United will be on high-alert after big West Ham news

West Ham United have sacked Nuno Espírito Santo after consecutive home defeats to fellow promotion hopefuls, Southampton and West Brom.

Now, all eyes will be on who shines under the new boss, who is set to be Scott Parker, and Leeds United loanee Joel Piroe may be one of them.

There were plenty of flaws with Nuno in the opening stages of the Championship, even if the Hammers had scored the most goals in the division and were among the early pace setters until this run of two straight defeats.

One of the main issues was his struggles coaching a side expected to have the ball, given the sheer quality of the West Ham squad compared to their second-tier counterparts.

Of their six league wins, five of them saw them keep their lowest possession numbers of the season. The other, against Lincoln City, serves as a clear outlier as they played against nine men for the majority of the game.

But what was arguably more concerning was that, barring Jarrod Bowen on the right and Arne Engels, who is the most expensive signing in Championship history, in the middle, there was hardly any consistency in Nuno's sides in terms of attacking personnel.

The striker position was the most egregious case of this. West Ham fans would head to games not knowing which two of Taty Castellanos, Pablo and Leeds loanee Joel Piroe would get the nod.

Pick any two players. Send the code, and your mate enters it here to play the same pair.

That's led to some disconnection up there, and is arguably the reason why, despite the strong goalscoring numbers, hardly any of them had come from those whose job it is to put the ball in the net.

Piroe leads the trio in scoring this season with three. But he's hardly been first choice. He's failed to start any more than two straight games, and he's come off the bench in each of the last three.

West Ham's loan capture of Piroe was as strong a sign as any that they'd be one of the strongest attacking sides in the Championship this season. The Surinamese international has been one of the best goalscorers in the second tier's recent history, both at Swansea City and Elland Road.

He's scored at least 19 times in three of his four full seasons at the level, the latter of which saw him win the Golden Boot en route to lifting the league title with his parent club.

Unfortunately, Piroe's style couldn't translate to the intense levels of the Premier League, which led him back to the top end of the Championship in a loan move which will become permanent for £12 million if West Ham get promoted.

With just two league starts in the 2025/26 campaign at Leeds, the move would have been facilitated to get two things over the line. A return to regular minutes and goalscoring form, and an avenue to start afresh with a new side if all went well at the London Stadium this year.

That's not happened under Nuno at all, and as it stands, the Whites will be set to bring Piroe back with his stock value even lower than it was this past summer. They'll be hoping that can change under Scott Parker, as and when he's given the job.

Parker's arrival at West Ham should get some Hammers fans who were dissatisfied with Nuno's reign back onside. Not only did he spend parts of his playing career at Upton Park, but he's got a perfect track record of securing promotion from this level.

The 46-year-old has taken Fulham, Bournemouth and, most recently, Burnley to the Premier League, the latter with record-breaking defensive numbers.

All three squads are more well-remembered for being difficult to score against, rather than outscoring opponents, and that's partially true. Burnley conceded 16 goals in 2024/25, Bournemouth had the best defensive record in 2021/22, and only the top three conceded fewer than his Fulham side in 2019/20.

However, it's not just defending that Parker sides are well-renowned for. Arguably, the fact he's been competing with some of the best attacking sides this division has ever seen in those two seasons has skewed some opinions.

Burnley scored 26 fewer than Leeds two years ago, but had the third-best goalscoring numbers. At Bournemouth, he finished second to Marco Silva's Fulham, who netted 106 times. In comparison, the Cherries' 74 goals aren't as good, but it was the second-best tally in the division.

Parker's sides have also benefitted from having a potent goalscorer, too. Whether that be Aleksandar Mitrovic's 26 in 2019/20 or Dominic Solanke's 29 a couple of years later.

How many goals do you think Joel Piroe could score in a Scott Parker setup? Let us know in the comments.

Even at Burnley, while Zian Flemming only scored 12, he played at least 1,000 minutes fewer than Mitrovic and Solanke in the aforementioned campaigns. When Flemming was the recognised number nine in 2026, he scored nine in 19.

So, with Parker's arrival to succeed Nuno seemingly imminent, it shouldn't be long until he starts to implement some of what has made his side so effective in this division, and that includes having one set striker to play through.

Piroe has been more of a link man in recent years at Leeds, but the 27-year-old has been at his best when leading the line. It was his performances as a striker which led the Whites to spend over £10 million on him in the summer of 2023.

AI has ranked the top 16 British football clubs and their hooligan firms.

If Scott Parker chooses the Surinamese international to be that focal point, rather than Taty Castellanos, he could well have a near-20-goal campaign once more at the level and contribute to another promotion.

That, ultimately, is what Leeds will want out of this managerial switch, as they'll be hoping they can rid themselves of Piroe permanently in the summer, as it's clear he won't have a Premier League future at Elland Road.

Perhaps both he and Scott Parker could prove some people wrong in 2027/28, though, if they both help the Hammers back to the top flight.

#2129. Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the new season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

Newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

Thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

Everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

The Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

It really should be 2-0 to Everton, a high-class moving down their left with Armstrong dinking a pass to Barry. He squared to Ndiaye who was free as a bird in the middle, but his shot was too close to Hornicek.

Joelinton runs down a blind alley before lumping a pass out for an Everton throw, and then the Newcastle man fouls Barry. The big Brazilian still finding his legs and getting up to speed.

A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

Ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

Half-hearted appeals for a penalty from Wissa, but Hayden Hackney did not do much wrong. Looks like we will be spared a first-half hydration break, despite it being a sultry evening.

Osula skips through a couple of challenges at the edge of the area but fails to pick a pass in the box. Bazoumana Touré has looked lively for Newcastle on their left flank, and Bamba has done well for them in midfield.

Everton shake themselves into life as an attacking force. Cracking cross from Patterson into the box and Dewsbury-Hall’s run had gone untracked, but he was just stretching and could not generate enough power to beat Hornicek.

Good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

Joelinton feeds Bamba down the left wing for Newcastle who delivers a cross into the penalty area. Keane can only direct his defensive header back towards the penalty spot, but Wissa volleyed over with a first-time hit. Decent chance.

Thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

Newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Big Dunc and Moyes catch up pre-match! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/Jh4APHOZvX

A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula

Newcastle subs: Gillespie, Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, M Miley, Finneran, Ramsey, Steur, Willock, J Murphy, Barnes, Neave, Woltemade

Your Mags at Murrayfield! ✊ pic.twitter.com/rDXpn0MqCg

Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry

Here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#2128. Jamie Carragher names Man Utd Star who impressed him against Leeds

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United had a difficult evening once again as they were held to a 1-1 draw at Leeds United. Pressure mounts on Michael Carrick as United have just 7 points from 7 games.

Manchester United took the lead through Bryan Mbeumo in the first half, with the forward finishing Youri Tielemans’ excellent cross from the right. However, the visitors couldn’t hold on to their advantage as Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised for Leeds United from a corner.

The draw extended United’s frustrating run of results, leaving Michael Carrick still searching for the consistency his side need.

Carragher, though, believes there were positives to take from the trip, particularly one performance at the back.

Jamie Carragher has singled out Harry Maguire for praise after Manchester United drew 1-1 with Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday.

Speaking on Sky Sports, the former Liverpool defender admitted that picking up a point at Elland Road was not necessarily a bad result in isolation, even if United’s recent form made it feel like a missed opportunity.

“Going away to Leeds is going to be tricky for any team except for Manchester City and Arsenal at the moment,” Carragher said.

“A lot of teams will take a point at Leeds this season but the problem for Manchester United is the results have been so poor that they need to start winning games so it almost feels like two points dropped.”

Carragher then turned his attention to Maguire, who he felt played a major role in keeping United in the game when Leeds began to push for a winner.

“But in isolation, getting a point at Leeds is a decent result. I thought Harry Maguire was fantastic, especially in the second half.”

Leeds United grew into the contest after Calvert-Lewin brought them level, putting United under pressure during the closing stages. Carragher felt Maguire’s efforts in defence helped prevent the visitors from falling apart.

“After Leeds got that goal back there was a stage of the game where it felt like Man United could go under, but Maguire at the back held it together for them. He was fantastic.”

The result may feel like another opportunity missed for Carrick, but Maguire’s performance gave United something positive to take away from Elland Road.

#2127. Kevin Nisbet's lack of cool proved so costly for Aberdeen at Hampden... and underlines why he's not a man for the big occasion

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 18:27 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 18:32 EDT, 31 October 2026

In the build-up to this Premier Sports Cup semi-final, Aberdeen captain Kevin Nisbet spoke about the players needing to step up and deliver.

On a woeful run of form as they arrived at Hampden, and with huge pressure mounting on Stephen Robinson, Nisbet insisted the players owed the manager a performance and a result.

Just to take the heat off as much as anything else. With 76 minutes on the clock in this tense and cagey affair with Rangers, Nisbet had a golden opportunity.

With the score locked at 0-0, Stuart Armstrong fed a pass into Nisbet’s path and the ball was crying out to be struck first time.

Nisbet could probably see the whites of Ivor Pandur’s eyes. In the context of the game, it was as good a chance as Aberdeen could have hoped for.

But his finish was absolutely awful. Nisbet hesitated when he should have pulled the trigger straight away, allowing Olwethu Makhanya to make a block.

Aberdeen striker Kevin Nisbet reflects on a golden chance to fire Aberdeen ahead at Hampden

On such moments are cup semi-finals won and lost. Just seven minutes later, at the other end of the pitch, Ryan Naderi prodded home from close range to send Rangers through to the final.

Nisbet will surely be haunted by his miss. He has scored 13 goals this season. For all Aberdeen’s struggles, some have even touted him for a Scotland recall.

But he is not up to scratch at the top level. In some respects, he finds himself in the same boat as Lawrence Shankland.

Any time Shankland has been given an opportunity with Scotland, he hasn’t really taken it. Particularly in the World Cup in the summer.

Nisbet is a decent enough striker at Scottish Professional Football League level. But in the big moments in big games, he’s not good enough.

It was a chance he had to take. In the end, Aberdeen were left to rue what might have been as Rangers, who were poor for much of the game, edged through to the final.

All in all, this is a defeat which just piles more pressure on Stephen Robinson. His team did not play poorly but they did not win.

Nisbet took too long with the ball and allowed Olwethu Makhanya the chance to block his shot

There is no sense in trotting out excuses about being competitive and unlucky. Aberdeen were not unlucky.

They had a glorious chance to go in front late in the game and their captain wasted it. That is not misfortune. It is profligacy.

Robinson and his players now face a huge game against Hibs at Pittodrie next Saturday.

With the international break just around the corner, a time when clubs invariably change manager once the rot has set in, it could well be last-chance saloon for Robinson.

#2126. Como vs Man Utd Preview: Team news, injuries, form and where to watch

Manchester United travel to Italy on Wednesday, looking for their first win since September 10, when they face Como in the Champions League.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to build any momentum this season. Sunday’s 1-1 draw against Leeds extended their winless run to six matches in all competitions, leaving United with just seven points from their opening seven Premier League games.

The pressure on Carrick continues to grow. A win in Europe would offer some relief, but Como will not make life easy for Manchester United.

Manchester United began their Champions League campaign with a convincing 4-0 win over Sabah FK but lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in their next match. They have since drawn with Leeds, having also failed to beat Fulham and Tottenham in the Premier League.

Their last six matches across all competitions have produced three draws and three defeats. Michael Carrick is in pressure of his own and needs a response from his players, particularly with United sitting 13th in the Premier League and 13th in the Champions League standings.

Como have shown more promise. Cesc Fabregas’ side beat RB Leipzig 4-1 in Europe before losing 3-2 to Feyenoord. They returned to winning ways against Fiorentina, claiming a 3-1 victory that moved them up to fifth in Serie A, with 14 points from seven games.

Como have scored 11 goals and conceded eight across their last six matches in all competitions. United have struggled, with their only clean sheet of the season coming against Sabah FK.

United have several confirmed absentees ahead of the trip to Italy. Patrick Dorgu, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko are ruled out, while Leny Yoro is suspended for the European fixture after picking a red against Atletico Madrid.

Lisandro Martinez is a major concern after coming off at half-time against Leeds with a thigh problem. Ayden Heaven, Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo are all doubtful for the game.

Como will be without Assane Diao, who is sidelined with a thigh injury. Moise Kean has a shin problem and is a doubt, while Trevoh Chalobah is also a fitness concern with a muscular issue.

The match takes place at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on Wednesday, October 21, with kick-off at 5:45 pm BST.

UK viewers can watch the Champions League fixture live on TNT Sports 2 and HBO Max.

#2125. West Ham can sack Scott Parker for free on one condition

Scott Parker is expected to become the latest head coach of West Ham United following the club's decision to dismiss Nuno Espírito Santo on Tuesday, but there is a catch to the looming appointment of the former midfielder.

Nuno saw the pressure on his shoulders grow even further on Saturday when the Hammers suffered a second straight Championship loss at the London Stadium at the hands of high-flying West Bromwich Albion.

The defeat against James Morrison's side also made it two games in succession where the Portuguese's side had shipped three goals in E20, having lost 3-2 to Southampton on October 24th.

Results elsewhere saw the East London side slide down to eighth in the table after 13 games played, with concerns raised about the fact the pre-season promotion favourites find themselves six points behind leaders Middlesbrough.

The timing of Nuno's decision did cause some form of surprise, though, with it being confirmed in Tuesday's early hours, less than 48 hours before the Hammers take on newly-promoted Cardiff City in South Wales.

Since then, it has been widely reported that Parker is to be who takes over, but a revelation about the deal he is set to sign has emerged.

Parker may have less than a decade's worth of managerial experience under his belt, but the former West Ham midfielder has achieved promotion in all of his three full seasons in the Championship with Fulham, AFC Bournemouth and Burnley.

However, he has also been unable to preserve the league status of two of those clubs, whilst he was dismissed by the Cherries shortly after promotion was achieved following a 9-0 hammering at Liverpool.

It has been reported by Hammers-related website, Claret and Hugh, that the 46-year-old is set to sign a two-and-a-half year contract with the club which would run until the summer of 2029.

However, there are serious short-term conditions which need to be met for Parker to fulfil the length of said contract, with the publication revealing that if a first-time promotion is not achieved, West Ham's board of directors have the capacity to relieve him of his duties at no cost.

If the club does return to the top-flight, though, Parker will be given the opportunity to stabilise the Hammers' position amongst English football's elite.

The Hammers have parted ways with the Portuguese head coach but are looking to act swiftly when sourcing his replacement

Parker's appointment would make him West Ham's 21st permanent manager, 14 months after Nuno signed a three-year contract in East London shortly after leaving Nottingham Forest.

The 52-year-old had won the Championship previously with Wolves, but despite winning 6-0 twice so far this season, sections of the fanbase had often voiced their frustrations at the Portuguese's tactics and overall performance levels.

#2123. Hibs' astonishing 47-year Hampden record vs Rangers sets up classic

Hibernian head into next month's Premier Sports Cup Final against Rangers with their tails up.

Granted the club's Scottish Premiership form leaves plenty to be desired, but their semi-final victory over fierce rivals Hearts on Sunday afternoon highlighted the fighting spirit still within the camp.

Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath's goals cancelled out Claudio Braga's early opener and set up the showpiece finale at Hampden Park on December 13. And it turns out Hibs have more to be excited and confident about given their history against the Light Blues at the national stadium.

Marink Reedijk's squad will square off against Derek McInnes' charges and they will do so with the bit between their teeth in the competition. But they also have history on their side.

Hibs have astonishingly not been beaten by Rangers at Hampden in a whopping 47 years.

The last time the Glasgow outfit came out on top was at the 1979 Scottish Cup final which took three attempts following a goalless draw in the initial final and then another in the replay. Rangers would win the third contest 3-2.

Since that period the two clubs have faced off four more times at Hampden and the Leith side have come out on top each time.

First came in the League Cup semi-final of 1991 when Keith Wright netted the winner inside the first 30 minutes. Then in 2004 Hibs progressed to the final of the same competition with a penalty shootout victory over their opponents following a 1-1 draw after extra-time. Stephen Dobbie had levelled after Michael Mols had opened the scoring for Gers during normal time.

The iconic 2016 Scottish Cup Final was next when former defender and then head coach David Gray bulleted home the winning header after an exhausting 3-2 victory for Hibs.

And in 2021 Hibs continued their reign of Hampden dominance over Rangers when they knocked them out of the League Cup at the semi-final stage again. Boyle fired in a stunning first-half hattrick before Scott Arfield nicked a consolation.

It's a staggering statistic and one Hibs will be desperate to add to when the final rolls around next month.

Michael Carrick has come under immense pressure as a disjointed Manchester United sit just two places above the relegation places.

Despite the scrutiny and the news of a possible sacking, Michael Carrick has been given another chance at Manchester United.

Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their Premier League trip to Chelsea on Saturday after the club decided to give their under-pressure head coach another opportunity to turn things around.

United have gone eight games without a win in all competitions, with Sunday’s humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth leaving them 16th in the Premier League table, just one point above the relegation zone.

Carrick’s position looked increasingly uncertain after the Bournemouth loss. As a result, United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were at Carrington on Monday to discuss the situation.

It has been reported by Sky Sports that United have considered other options internally as well to replace Micahel Carrick but for the weekend, they are sticking with Michael Carrick.

Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision means he has at least one more match to convince the club’s hierarchy that he can get United back on track.

Gary Neville admitted he was surprised that Carrick had survived the immediate threat of losing his job, although he welcomed the decision.

#2121. Middlesbrough's £20m Will Lankshear gamble has a hidden upside

Middlesbrough have struck gold with their Will Lankshear signing from Tottenham Hotspur, with the young striker already looking like one of the Championship's outstanding acquisitions.

It is only early November, yet the 21-year-old has scored 13 league goals and 15 in all competitions for Kim Hellberg's side. That is five more than any other Championship player this season already.

In fact, only seven players across the entire 2025/26 campaign managed to outscore his current league tally. Middlesbrough's investment is already looking inspired, but there is an interesting financial detail behind the deal to consider.

Lankshear's spectacular brace against Charlton Athletic provided another reminder of just how special a finisher Middlesbrough have acquired. Both goals were excellent left-footed efforts, although the second was arguably the finest of his professional career to date.

He is making an extraordinary impact at the Riverside Stadium, and the reported £10 million initial fee, as per BBC Sport, is already looking like outstanding business. However, the widely reported £20 million headline figure includes approximately £10 million in potential add-ons, meaning Boro are not necessarily committed to paying the full amount.

If they do, it will be a club-record deal. The exact conditions of that have not been publicly confirmed yet, but they could — and indeed are likely to include — appearances, goals, assists, promotion from the Championship, and potentially even international recognition, such as an England call-up.

There is often a downside to these arrangements, with clubs sometimes finding themselves committed to expensive conditional payments or future obligations that eat into subsequent transfer budgets. That's an inherently risky strategy for any club, let alone ones without parachute payments aiding them. Yet Lankshear could be a very different proposition for Boro.

If Middlesbrough are paying those additional sums because he has helped them achieve major sporting objectives, particularly promotion, then the extra money will hardly represent a costly mistake. It should actually feel like a drop in the ocean to them on current trajectory.

In fact, a young English striker who fires Boro into the Premier League would suddenly be worth considerably more than £20 million, making those add-ons a relatively small price to pay for an extraordinary investment. Spurs are protected somewhat by matching rights for Lankshear, but while hindsight is a wonderful thing, it's already looking like a far better deal for Boro than Tottenham as time goes by.

Lankshear's may be killing it for Middlesbrough but his development has not been entirely straightforward, with his first Championship loan at West Bromwich Albion failing to deliver the impact he would have wanted in January 2025 for half a season.

However, his subsequent spell at Oxford United was considerably more productive, scoring 12 goals despite playing for a side that created relatively little and ultimately suffered relegation to League One back in May.

His story is a reminder that development is rarely linear, and he is now demonstrating exactly why Tottenham invested so heavily in him as a youngster. Under Hellberg, Lankshear looks like the division's best natural finisher and penalty-box poacher, too. Their attack-minded style of play means he is guaranteed plenty of chances.

If he maintains this form and stays fit, he could even start to eye up and begin dreaming of challenging Aleksandar Mitrovic's extraordinary Championship record of 43 goals in a single season for Fulham. That remains a monumental target, but his start has been outstanding.

There is also a potentially significant international dimension to Lankshear's development. He has the profile to become a serious England contender, with the long-term ambition of eventually succeeding Harry Kane as the national team's leading centre-forward.

There are not many players worthy of competing with Kane, but Lankshear is on the right path. The parallels are interesting, too, given Kane's own progression through a series of EFL loan spells before establishing himself at Tottenham.

The difference is that Spurs have now cashed in on Lankshear rather than sending him out on another temporary deal. His finishing repertoire is already impressive, having scored regularly with both feet and his head this season. He is becoming a remarkably complete penalty-box striker.

Spurs correspondent and journalist Alasdair Gold has even hinted at the Kane-esque comparison recently after seeing Lankshear's strike against the Addicks. It's fair to say that if Lankshear continues on this trajectory, Tottenham could eventually find themselves collecting those add-ons through his England progress as well as the aforementioned club achievements.

Not only that, but they would be a Premier League club again, meaning they would have Lankshear to face the likes of Spurs and Arsenal and prove a point to two north London clubs that let him go in his early career.
